items.title: Iran warns against ground invasion as diplomats meet in Pakistan

featured_image.name: Pakistan maintains 'delicate balancing act' as it hosts Iran talks

items.description:
Foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt gathered in Islamabad on Sunday for a two-day summit aimed at charting a path toward ending the month-long war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, even as fighting continued and Tehran publicly rejected the terms on offer. Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar is leading the talks, which officials have described as the most coordinated regional diplomatic effort since the conflict began on February 28.[1][2][3]

Neither the United States, Iran, nor Israel is participating in the meetings. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said the goal was to open "direct dialogue" between Washington and Tehran, which have so far communicated only through intermediaries. Turkey's Hakan Fidan and Saudi Arabia's Prince Faisal bin Farhan rounded out the gathering, which Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif set up after holding what he called "extensive discussions" with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday.[3][4][5]

items.title: Satellite images show 88 structures destroyed at key Iran missile site

featured_image.name: Iran ballistic missiles sites severely damaged by U.S., Israeli strikes -  The Washington Post

items.description: A month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, a Washington Post analysis of satellite imagery published Saturday found that four of Iran's key ballistic missile manufacturing sites have suffered severe damage, with at least 88 structures destroyed at the Khojir Aerospace Complex alone. Yet U.S. intelligence assessments reveal that only about one-third of Iran's missile arsenal has been confirmed destroyed, and Tehran continues to launch missiles across the region.[1][2]

items.title: Netanyahu orders expansion of Israel's ground invasion in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Netanyahu: War against Iran 'continuing with full force ...

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced Sunday that Israel will expand its ground invasion of southern Lebanon, ordering the military to broaden what he called the "existing security strip" as fighting with the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militant group enters its fourth week.

"We are determined to fundamentally change the situation in the north," Netanyahu said during a visit to northern Israel, adding that "Hezbollah still has residual capability to fire rockets at us."[1][2][3]

No immediate details were provided on how far the expanded zone would reach.

items.title: Pentagon prepares ground operations in Iran as war enters 30th day

featured_image.name: 2,200 US Marines to arrive in Middle East on March 27 on ...

items.description: Approximately 3,500 U.S. Marines and sailors aboard the amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli arrived in the Middle East on March 27, U.S. Central Command confirmed Saturday, as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran enters its 30th day with mounting signs of escalation. Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf responded with a stark warning, saying Iranian forces "are waiting for the arrival of American troops on the ground to set them on fire and punish their regional partners forever".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Ukrainian drones crash in Finland, extending NATO airspace breaches

featured_image.name: Two unidentified drones crash in southeastern Finland in 'suspected  territorial violation'

items.description: Two drones crashed in southeastern Finland near the city of Kouvola on Sunday morning, in what the country's defence ministry described as a "suspected territorial violation" — the latest in a string of incidents in which Ukrainian strike drones have veered into NATO territory amid intensifying attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.

items.title: Study pinpoints sun's storm engine 200,000 km below surface

featured_image.name: Visualization of the solar interior with the tachocline | Instituto de  Astrofísica de Canarias • IAC

items.description: Physicists at the New Jersey Institute of Technology have pinpointed the origin of solar storms to a thin boundary layer buried roughly 200,000 kilometers beneath the sun's visible surface, providing the first direct observational evidence that this region drives the star's magnetic activity cycle.

items.title: North Korea tests upgraded missile engine with higher thrust

featured_image.name: North Korea's Kim oversees ground test of new high-thrust missile engine:  KCNA

items.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un supervised a ground test of a newly upgraded high-thrust solid-fuel missile engine, state media reported on Sunday, marking a step forward in the country's drive to bolster its long-range strike capabilities.

items.title: WTO talks enter final day with U.S., India deadlocked on e-commerce duties

featured_image.name: WTO talks stalled going into final day amid U.S.-India e-commerce deadlock

items.description:
Talks at the World Trade Organization's 14th Ministerial Conference in Yaoundé, Cameroon, entered their final day on Sunday with no breakthrough in sight over extending a moratorium on customs duties for electronic transmissions, as the United States and India remain far apart on the issue, diplomats told Reuters.[1]

The e-commerce moratorium, which has been in place since 1998 and bars countries from imposing customs duties on digital downloads and other electronic transmissions, is set to expire at the end of March. Its extension is widely seen as a litmus test for the WTO's continued relevance amid a year of tariff-fueled trade turmoil and disruptions stemming from the conflict in the Middle East.[2][3][1]

items.title: Iran hits Abu Dhabi smelter, Saudi base as war widens across Gulf

featured_image.name: Emirates Global Aluminium Al Taweelah site damaged in Iranian missile, drone attacks

items.description: The war between the United States and Israel against Iran intensified sharply on Friday as Israel launched airstrikes on Iranian nuclear facilities and weapons factories, while Iran struck back across the Persian Gulf, wounding 12 American service members at a Saudi air base and damaging a major aluminum smelter in Abu Dhabi. The escalation came as the conflict entered its fifth week with no ceasefire in sight and new actors — including Yemen's Houthi rebels — joining the fight.

items.title: Iran hits Bahrain refinery, aluminum smelter near US base

featured_image.name: Dozens Wounded in Bahrain as Arab States Condemn Iranian ...

items.description: Massive fires erupted at industrial facilities across Bahrain on Saturday after Iranian missile and drone strikes targeted the BAPCO oil refinery in the Sitra/Al-Ma'ameer industrial district, the Aluminium Bahrain (ALBA) smelter, and areas adjacent to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters in Al Juffair. The attacks mark one of the most intense single-day escalations against Bahrain since Iran began retaliating against joint US-Israeli strikes that commenced on February 28.

items.title: ESA launches first Celeste satellites to bolster navigation

featured_image.name: ESA - ESA's Celeste target launch date confirmed

items.description: The European Space Agency on Saturday launched the first two satellites of its Celeste mission, opening a new chapter in European satellite navigation as the agency moves to complement its Galileo system with a closer-to-Earth constellation.

items.title: Houthis launch second attack on Israel within 24 hours, vow more strikes

featured_image.name: Houthis claim missile launch at Israel amid renewed fighting in Gaza

items.description:
Yemen's Houthi rebels carried out a second attack on Israel using missiles and drones on Saturday, less than 24 hours after their first strike, formally entering the month-old US-Israeli war against Iran and opening yet another front in a rapidly expanding regional conflict.

The group's military spokesman, Brigadier General Yahya Saree, announced the second assault in a televised address on the Houthis' Al-Masirah satellite channel, vowing to continue military operations in the coming days. Reuters reported that the Iran-aligned group used both missiles and unmanned aircraft in the second wave.[1][2]

items.title: Kyushu University achieves 130% quantum yield in solar breakthrough

featured_image.name: Singlet fission breaks 'ceiling' of solar cells for 130% quantum yield

items.description: A flurry of breakthroughs in solar cell research is challenging assumptions about how much energy photovoltaic technology can extract from sunlight. In findings published this week, researchers at Kyushu University in Japan and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz in Germany achieved a quantum yield of roughly 130 percent — meaning more energy carriers were produced than photons absorbed — while a separate team at the Chinese Academy of Sciences reached a power conversion efficiency of 29.76 percent for all-perovskite tandem solar cells.

items.title: Houthis enter Iran war as attacks sweep Gulf states

featured_image.name: At least 15 US troops wounded in Iran strike on Saudi airbase: Reports

items.description:
An Iranian missile and drone attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia on Friday wounded at least 12 American service members and damaged multiple U.S. military aircraft, marking one of the most serious breaches of American air defenses since the war began a month ago. Two of the wounded were listed in serious condition, according to U.S. officials cited by The New York Times and Reuters.[1][2]

The assault on the base south of Riyadh involved ballistic missiles and drones, with at least two missiles and one drone bypassing U.S. air defenses, according to officials. Multiple KC-135 aerial refueling tankers were damaged, and an E-3 Sentry AWACS command-and-control aircraft also sustained damage, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported. Iran publicized satellite imagery it said showed burning aircraft at the base. By Saturday, the total number of injuries had risen to around two dozen, with most of the additional cases attributed to traumatic brain injuries, according to The New York Times.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Vance says US will leave Iran 'soon' as Tehran rejects peace talks

featured_image.name: JD Vance is walking a tightrope on Iran. What does he really think?

items.description:
Vice President JD Vance said on Saturday that the United States has achieved most of its military objectives in Iran and plans to leave "soon," even as Tehran publicly denies that any meaningful peace negotiations are underway, one month into the conflict that has roiled global energy markets.

Speaking in an interview with conservative podcaster Benny Johnson, Vance acknowledged the war's economic toll but framed it as fleeting. "This is a very, very temporary reaction to what is ultimately going to be a short-term conflict," he said, referring to soaring energy prices caused by the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz. He added that President Trump "has been very clear" the administration has no interest in a prolonged presence: "We're not interested in being in Iran a year down the road, two years down the road. We're taking care of business, we're going to be out of there soon, and gas prices are going to come back down."[1][2][3]

Yet Vance also signaled that the campaign is not over. "The president's going to keep at it for a little while longer to ensure that once we leave, we don't have to do this again for a very, very long time," he said. "We need to neuter them for a very, very long time, and that's the purpose."[1]

items.title: Houthis launch first missile attack on Israel as U.S. Marines reach Middle East

featured_image.name: U.S. to Deploy Marines to Middle East. Here's What They Could Be ...

items.description:
The USS Tripoli and roughly 2,500 Marines arrived in the Middle East on Friday as Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen launched their first missile attack on Israel since the war began, opening a new front in a rapidly expanding regional conflict now one month old.

U.S. Central Command announced Saturday that the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group and the embarked 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit reached its area of responsibility on March 27, carrying approximately 3,500 sailors and Marines along with strike fighter aircraft and amphibious assault assets. The America-class amphibious assault ship had departed its homeport of Sasebo, Japan, earlier this month after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth approved a CENTCOM request for reinforcements.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: WHO says nine paramedics killed in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israel Killed Over a Dozen Lebanese Paramedics in Three Days ...

items.description:
The World Health Organization said Saturday that nine paramedics were killed and seven others wounded in five separate attacks on healthcare teams in southern Lebanon, bringing the total number of health workers killed since the Israeli military escalation began on March 2 to 51.[1][2]

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus detailed the strikes in a post on X, saying medics were hit while on duty in five villages. In Zoutar al-Sharqiya, five health workers were killed and two injured, one critically. Two more were killed and three wounded in Kfar Tibnit. One paramedic died in each of Ghandouriyeh and Jezzine, while two were wounded in Kfar Dajjal.[2][3]

"The repeated attacks on health care are severely disrupting the delivery of services in southern Lebanon," Tedros wrote, adding that "the only way to end these tragedies is to end attacks on health care, NOW".[2]

items.title: Drone strike hits Kurdistan president's home in Duhok

featured_image.name: Iraq Says Drone Attack Targeted Kurdistan President's Home

items.description: A drone strike targeted the residence of Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani in the northern Iraqi city of Duhok on Saturday, prompting Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani to condemn what he called a "brutal attack" and order an immediate investigation, according to Reuters. No casualties were reported.[1][2]

items.title: China launches world's first floating deep-sea research island in Shanghai

featured_image.name: China launches world's first floating deep-sea research island

items.description: China officially launched the world's first ultra-large floating deep-sea research facility in Shanghai on Saturday, the same week a Reuters investigation revealed that dozens of Chinese research vessels have been systematically mapping the ocean floor across the Pacific, Indian, and Arctic oceans in what naval experts say is preparation for potential submarine warfare against the United States and its allies.

items.title: Rosatom says Bushehr nuclear plant situation worsening after third strike

featured_image.name: Iran says nuclear facilities hit by strikes after Israel ...

items.description: A series of strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities in recent days, including the country's only operational nuclear power plant, have intensified international alarm over the risk of a radiological incident, even as authorities report no radiation leaks so far.
